verdict.reason:
The defect is real and the cited cause is right.

**The quotes appear.** I re-rendered tools/battles/2026-11-10_2209.bcb and all three quotes appear word for word in the Tipper, Janovec and Davenport sections. Randleman gets the same "two others" plus "He also brought down an E8N floatplane." The original crew-reports.txt log from the game has the same lumping, so this is not something the converter approximates.

**What the "others" really are.** The kill lines in the log give:
- Tipper: 3 sub chasers, 2 patrol boats, 1 tanker and the Japanese Merchant Type B. His "one other" is the merchant ship.
- Davenport: 3 patrol boats, 4 sub chasers, 3 tankers, the E8N and the merchant. His "two others" are the E8N and the merchant.
- Randleman: the same two others as Davenport.
- Janovec: his "one other" is the E8N, which the sentence just before names.

**Why this is wrong, not a matter of taste.**
- The merchant ship is never named in the Tipper, Davenport or Randleman sections. Tipper's single leftover type could have been named in the same space it takes to say "one other".
- For Davenport and Randleman, the plane is already counted among the "two others". "He also brought down an E8N floatplane" then reads as a kill on top of the twelve (or eleven), which double-counts it.

**The cause is right.**
- In the 5+ kills branch, RenderKills keeps the top 3 types and lumps the rest into "N other(s)" (`if (listed < n) items.push_back(... " other" ...)`, about line 1904).
- The leftover pass only names a non-top-3 kill through kill.plane or kill.big. BigRank uses a substring match against the [big] list (Cruiser, Destroyer, Transport, Tanker, Freighter, Maru, Supply, Minesweeper, Chaser). None of those words is in "Japanese Merchant Type B Sugar Baker Love", so BigRank returns -1 and the merchant is never named. The 2149 render shows the same gap: its summary says "among them a minesweeper" although a merchant ship was also sunk.

**The weak part.** That 2149 summary claim, and the claim that the merchant is the biggest ship sunk, are softer: "among them" does not claim to be complete. The core defects above stand without them.

quote: By the end Heavy had a hand in five kills: five enemy vessels. Every one of them was hers alone.
problem: Redundant wording ("five kills: five enemy vessels"). It is also odd that a damage-control hand with no gun has five lone kills.

ShipOf("") gives the generic "enemy vessel(s)", so the type list only repeats the count. A careful reader sees "five kills: five enemy vessels" as saying the same thing twice, not as a matter of taste.

quote: A minute later the torpedo blast hurled her against the bridge, ... (03:21). A minute later she was dragged back over the rail, coughing, ...
problem: Repetition. Two consecutive sentences open with "A minute later".
cause: The [over.pulled] row "{Dur} later ..." (line 652) builds its own relative phrase from Dur(). x.p->lastRel (line 1466) only guards When().
fix: In the S_PULLED/S_UP case (lines 1772-1792), skip rows starting "{Dur} later" when CapFirst(Dur(d)) + " later" equals the last relative phrase. Or set x.p->lastRel after Dur and compare it.

verdict.reason:
The defect is real. I ran tools/out/crew_report_test.exe on the synthetic battles, and Ann Gray's paragraph contains the quote word for word: "A minute later the torpedo blast hurled her against the bridge, ... over the side (03:21). A minute later she was dragged back over the rail, coughing, and was soon back at the Lewis (04:20)."

Two sentences in a row opening with the same phrase is a real defect, not a matter of taste. The renderer is written to prevent exactly this: line 1466 has the guard `if (ph == x.p->lastRel) ph.clear(); // never the same relative phrase twice running`. The battle is synthetic, so none of the converter's known approximations apply.

The cited cause is right:
- The first "A minute later" comes from When(), which sets x.p->lastRel (line 1468).
- The second comes from the [over.pulled] row "{Dur} later {he} was dragged back over the rail, coughing." Here {Dur} is CapFirst(Dur(d)). Dur() returns "a minute" for 40 to 75 s, and the gap here is 03:21 to 04:20, about 59 s.
- The S_PULLED case never compares or updates lastRel, so the guard is bypassed.

The same gap exists in S_UP, via {Dur} rows in down.up such as "A few seconds later she was back on her feet". The suggested fix of comparing CapFirst(Dur(d)) + " later" with lastRel is sound.
